input.quote: 2.2 Vendor will be Customer's sole and exclusive provider of hosted analytics services throughout the term.
input.rationale:
Section 2.2 binds Customer to use Vendor as its sole and exclusive provider of hosted analytics for the entire term, with no category carve-outs and no performance-based exit — this is the walk-away position under the rule (exclusive dealing for the full term without a service-level/delivery exit), and it fails even the 12-month, performance-terminable fallback. It also directly contradicts Section 12.3 (p0049), in which Vendor acknowledges Customer has made no exclusivity commitment, creating an interpretive conflict that should be resolved in favour of the no-exclusivity position. Redline makes the appointment non-exclusive (preferred position); a 12-month, category-limited exclusivity with automatic termination on SLA/delivery failure is offered as fallback in the comment.</parationale>
<parameter name="confidence">0.9

proposal.summary: Make Vendor's appointment non-exclusive and confirm Customer may source elsewhere
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We cannot commit to Copperleaf as our sole and exclusive provider for the full term, so we have made the appointment non-exclusive; this also removes the conflict with Section 12.3, which already confirms we have given no exclusivity commitment. If some exclusivity is important to you, we could discuss a 12-month term limited to hosted analytics that ends automatically if service levels or delivery dates are missed.

ops.oldText: 2.2 Vendor will be Customer's sole and exclusive provider of hosted analytics services throughout the term.
ops.newText: 2.2 Vendor's appointment is non-exclusive. Customer may obtain hosted analytics services, or any other products or services, from any third party at any time.
